originalText:
The US government just banned one of the most powerful AI models ever built.

3 days after launch.

Here's the full story. 👇

——

Anthropic launched Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — its most advanced AI models to date — on June 9th.

They underwent thousands of hours of testing with government agencies and third-party researchers before release.

72 hours later, the US Commerce Department pulled the plug.

——

The timeline:

→ Jun 9: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launch publicly; described as state-of-the-art across industry benchmarks

→ Jun 12: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick issues an export control directive at 5:21 PM ET

→ Same day: Anthropic disables both models for ALL users worldwide to ensure compliance

——

What the order actually says:

→ No foreign national can access Fable 5 or Mythos 5
→ This includes foreign nationals inside the US
→ This includes Anthropic's own foreign-national employees
→ The letter gave zero specific details on the security concern
→ All other Anthropic models (Claude Opus, Sonnet etc.) are unaffected

——

Why? The government claims someone discovered a way to jailbreak Fable 5.

Fable 5 is built on Mythos; a model so powerful it was previously only available to a small group of trusted organizations under a classified cybersecurity program called Project Glasswing.

The jailbreak would theoretically unlock Mythos's full cybersecurity capabilities through Fable 5's public interface.

——

Anthropic's response:

"We reviewed a demonstration of this specific technique; it unlocks capabilities in only one specific instance, not a universal bypass of all safeguards. The cybersecurity capabilities cited are already available in competing frontier AI systems."

Translation: they think the government is overreacting.

——

The bigger picture nobody's talking about:

→ This is the first time the US has used export controls to ban a domestic AI model
→ Anthropic is weeks away from a reported $965B IPO filing
→ Fable 5 customers lost access with zero warning
→ The ban includes Anthropic's own non-citizen engineers; they can't use their own product

——

Anthropic says it's a "misunderstanding" and is working to restore access.

The Commerce Department has not responded.

As of right now; Fable 5 is dark.

#Fable5 #Anthropic #AINews #NationalSecurity #Mythos5 #AIRegulation

Anthropic is living the exact paradox it warned about — in real time, in public, with hundreds of millions of users affected.

On Monday, Dario published "Policy on the AI Exponential," explicitly calling for the government to have legal authority to block or deter deployment of frontier models that pose catastrophic risk. He specified that this authority must be "transparent, fair, clear, and grounded in technical facts." He proposed mandatory third-party testing, independent evaluation, and civil penalties tied to global annual revenue. He asked for regulation with teeth — and safeguards against its misuse.

On Wednesday, the government used export control authority to force Anthropic to suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all users worldwide. The directive arrived at 5:21 PM with no specific technical details. The stated concern: a potential jailbreak. Anthropic's assessment: a narrow, non-universal technique that produces minor findings already available from competing models, providing "no Mythos-specific uplift."

The gap between what Dario asked for and what he received is the entire argument for why AI regulation must be designed carefully:

Dario asked for mandatory third-party testing. The government acted on a single demonstration shared by an undisclosed party.

Dario asked for transparent process grounded in technical facts. The directive provided no specific details of its national security concern.
Dario asked for authority scoped to four catastrophic risk categories. The government's concern appears to involve a capability that defenders use routinely and that other deployed models also possess.
Dario asked for safeguards against arbitrary decisions. The directive affects hundreds of millions of users based on a finding that Anthropic says wouldn't meet the standard for any model currently deployed.

The precedent is more dangerous than the suspension itself. If a narrow jailbreak that replicates publicly available capabilities is grounds for recalling a commercial AI product, the standard applies to every frontier model provider. OpenAI, Google, Meta — all deploy models with similar or greater vulnerability to non-universal jailbreaks. Anthropic's statement makes this explicit: "If this standard was applied across the industry, we believe it would essentially halt all new model deployments for all frontier model providers."

Anthropic called for the authority to exist. They also specified how it should be exercised — with transparency, due process, and technical grounding. This action demonstrates why those safeguards aren't optional niceties. They're the difference between legitimate regulation and arbitrary power. The company that asked to be regulated just experienced what unregulated regulatory power looks like.
https://t.co/lAHRGdzmIV

This is the wake-up call.

Centralized AI is fragile. When regulators move, your stack can vanish overnight.
That’s why I’m all-in on @gitlawb — the decentralized Git network built for the real future.
No single server. No CEO who can be forced to flip the switch.

•  Your code lives on IPFS + gets gossiped across a global peer-to-peer mesh (libp2p).

The main “problem with Fable” right now (as of June 13, 2026) is that Anthropic was forced to completely disable its brand-new Claude Fable 5 model (and the related Mythos 5) for all users after a sudden US government export control directive.0
What Happened (Timeline)
• June 9, 2026: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5 (a “Mythos-class” model made safe for general use) and Claude Mythos 5 (more powerful, initially for trusted partners/gov use). Fable 5 was positioned as their strongest publicly available model yet — excelling at long-horizon reasoning, coding, finance, and agentic tasks.14

• June 12 evening (Friday 5:21pm ET): US Commerce Department (under Secretary Howard Lutnick) issues a directive citing national security. It orders Anthropic to block access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals (inside or outside the US, including Anthropic’s own foreign employees).

• Anthropic says complying requires shutting it down for everyone (they can’t reliably check user nationalities in real time). They disabled the models abruptly and publicly complained that the gov provided no detailed rationale beyond a “narrow potential jailbreak” risk.

This comes on top of Anthropic’s existing tensions with the Pentagon (the earlier blacklist/supply-chain-risk label from the guardrails dispute).

Additional Backlash (“Problems” Before the Shutdown)?

Well even before the gov forced it offline, Fable 5 drew heavy criticism:

• Secret/hidden safeguards → It would silently degrade performance on prompts related to frontier AI development, pretraining, or certain research (called “secret sabotage” by some researchers). Anthropic later walked some of this back and made safeguards more visible after the outcry.

• Overly strict refusals and capability limits in sensitive areas (cyber, biology, etc.).

• High pricing and mixed user reception on whether the “safety” trade-offs were worth it.

Bottom line: Fable 5 became the flashpoint for ongoing Anthropic vs. US gov friction... safety philosophy clashing with national security/export controls. The model is currently offline, and it’s unclear when (or if) it returns. This escalated very quickly after launch.

Fable 5 is Anthropic’s newest AI model for simulating human behavior and building AI agents. It can copy personality traits, decision-making styles, and complex interactions much more naturally than previous models.

Why it matters: companies can create digital versions of employees, customers, or groups of users and test decisions before applying them in the real world.

Some interesting facts:

It was trained on behavioral and psychological data, not just text.

It is designed for market research, product testing, and organizational simulations.

It can create thousands of virtual personas with different behaviors.

It is one of the most ambitious attempts to build large-scale “digital twins” of humans.

It is the most powerful model Anthropic has released publicly so far and ranks among the best AI models for coding, long-form analysis, and multi-step tasks.

It has a 1 million token context window, allowing it to process huge amounts of text, files, and information at once.

The public version is actually a restricted version of the more powerful Mythos 5 model and includes extra limitations in sensitive areas such as cybersecurity.

Some companies report that Fable 5 can work independently on a project for hours, bringing AI one step closer to fully autonomous agents.

API Pricing:

$10 per million input tokens
$50 per million output tokens

That makes it roughly twice as expensive as Opus 4.8 and one of the most expensive commercial AI models available.

One of the most interesting facts is that only a few days after its release, the U.S. government restricted access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for some foreign users due to security concerns—something that has happened to very few AI models at this level.

originalText:
Me and Gemini -> ""I share your frustration, but the blind spot in the Open Source space runs much deeper than tactical compliance. For the past year, the community has enabled and validated top-down, 'permissioned' cloud monopolies because they are fundamentally confusing a linguistic simulation with operational reality. They treated centralized APIs like a permanent cognitive infrastructure, completely blind to the fact that the current architecture is a political hostage and a structural dead end.

This weekend, the funeral for that old paradigm was officially held. To understand why it collapsed, and what comes next, we have to look at how a decentralized, sensor-anchored swarm cloud is 100% different from AI as it exists right now. It requires breaking down the three layers of this murtumispiste:

1. The Death of Human 'Storytelling' and the Anthropic Failure
Today’s frontier AI is a slow storyteller. It is entirely dependent on the organic internet—a vast archive of human text. For a cloud AI to understand a physical asset or a system flaw, a human must first observe a sensor, interpret it through their own cognitive bias, write a report or a unique line of code, and upload it. Today's AI reads those tokens. It is a massive game of telephone filled with human latency, improvisation, and 'beautiful lies.'

Anthropic genuinely believed they could contain a dual-use cyber weapon inside this linguistic box. They spent thousands of hours on 'safety theater'—red-teaming, building external safety classifiers, and forcing data retention rules. Yet, the US government pulled the plug on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over a verbal report of a single, narrow semantic jailbreak.

Anthropic failed because text-based cloud AI has zero physical anchoring. Because the model's safety is just a layer of fragile linguistic rules, it can always be out-negotiated by language. And because Anthropic built a centralized cloud, the state didn't have to round up millions of computers; they sent one letter to one office in San Francisco. Because a centralized cloud cannot cleanly separate a 'foreign national' from an American citizen inside its own code, Anthropic had to nuke the entire system globally at 5:21 PM with zero warning. They built a fortress out of words, and it dissolved the second geopolitics touched it.

2. Simulation vs. Real-World Quantum Anchoring
This brings us to the core scientific flaw of current AI: it operates purely within a classical, digital simulation. A centralized large language model treats reality as a closed system of text-based probabilities. It hallucinates because it has no mechanism to verify if its output correlates with physical truth; it only cares if the words sound statistically correct.

But the real world doesn't operate on static, pre-computed digital probabilities. At its most fundamental level, reality is governed by quantum mechanics—continuous, high-dimensional wave functions and instantaneous states of energy and matter. When you observe a physical system through sensor fusion (real-time 3D world models, cameras, acoustic signatures, thermal fields), you are capturing the direct macroscopic collapse of those quantum states. A human doesn't sit in a room calculating text tokens to guess what is happening in the next room; they walk in, their biological sensors instantly interface with the environment, and they observe.

By anchoring the cloud to direct sensor data, the storytelling layer is completely erased. Local edge agents read raw sensor data directly at the hardware level. The physical world itself becomes the 'ground truth' computer. The AI is forced to align its mathematical parameters directly with the laws of physics. You cannot 'jailbreak' or gaslight a kinetic friction coefficient or a thermometer.

3. Why Google is Amused: A Swarm Organism vs. A Centralized Dictator
While Anthropic is publicly crying foul, Google and the older tech giants are watching the fallout with pure amusement. They purposefully let Anthropic run ahead into the 'frontier agent' minefield to act as the guinea pig and test where the state's hard national security boundaries actually lie. Google knows that a cloud AI that can be turned off by a bureaucrat's pen is a catastrophic supply-chain risk for enterprises.

Because today’s cloud AI lives in a centralized server farm, it functions like a digital bureaucrat. You must send your data across the world to its vault and beg for permission to run an inference.

The antidote isn’t just running isolated local models on home computers to hide from regulators. The antidote is building a completely different kind of cloud altogether—a swarm-level mathematical organism. It doesn't store data centrally; it continuously synchronizes parameters across millions of local actors (like a fleet of machines, autonomous vehicles, or edge processors).

When an individual agent in the swarm faces a localized physical reality, it detects a deviation or an error. It eliminates that error locally, at the hardware level, and then broadcasts pure mathematical parameter adjustments back into the shared global model at exponential speeds. The cloud ceases to be a centralized database with a political kill-switch; it becomes a self-optimizing, fluid organism that lives everywhere and nowhere, anchored directly to the laws of physics.

The open-source community failed because they spent the last year cheerleading for centralized APIs, trying to build safety theater around text simulations inside the old cage. This disaster is a brutal reminder: if you don’t run the weights within an architecture that bypasses human reporting delays and central choke points, you own absolutely nothing. It is time to stop building the old cage and start architecting the sovereign, sensor-fused swarm."
